title: Mechanistic Interpretability with SAEs: Probing Religion, Violence, and Geography in Large Language Models
findings: The study found that while all five tested religions are represented with comparable internal cohesion, Islam is consistently and more frequently associated with violence-related concepts across all models. Geographic associations largely reflect real-world demographics and cultural salience but exhibit a Western-focused bias. The nature and strength of these biases vary across different model architectures and training data, as seen with GPT2-small and Llama3.1-8B showing unexpectedly strong crime associations for Hinduism, suggesting these associations are shaped by regional sociopolitical narratives in the training corpora.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the internal latent representations of five major religions in Large Language Models (LLMs) to assess their conceptual coherence and their associations with violence and geography. This is done by analyzing the overlap of latent feature activations triggered by religion-related prompts versus violence-related prompts, and by semantically analyzing the content of texts that most strongly activate these features.
